# 0011. Translation types generated by a separate run

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-30

## Context

The 2026-10-26 amendment of [ADR 0009](0009-i18next.md) generates translation types with `i18next-cli extract --with-types`. That flag runs the type generator only when extraction changed a translation file. After a hand edit of the locale files, extraction has nothing to change, so `web/src/i18n/resources.d.ts` stays stale. `tsc` notices only when code uses a new key, never when an existing text changed, and the `generated` CI job sees no difference.

## Decision

- `pnpm i18n:extract` runs `i18next-cli extract && i18next-cli types`, so `task generate` always rewrites the types from the English locale files.
- This supersedes the sentence on `extract --with-types` in the 2026-10-26 amendment of ADR 0009. The rest of ADR 0009 stands.

## Consequences

- The `generated` CI job fails when the committed types are out of date.
- `web/i18n-extract.test.ts` runs the script on a copy of the web app, so going back to `--with-types` fails a test.
- `i18next-cli types` exits with 0 when it fails. The script relies on `extract` running first, which exits with 1 on a malformed translation file.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep `--with-types` and add `i18next-cli types --ci` to `pnpm i18n:check`**: detects stale types, but `task generate` still would not repair them. Rejected, because generated files should come from `task generate` alone.
